thread.title: Rep. Chris Smith calls for stronger enforcement of Uyghur labor law on imported toys
thread.title_full: Rep. Chris Smith calls for stronger enforcement of Uyghur labor law on imported toys

author: m. y. simpkins
title: Rep. Chris Smith calls for stronger enforcement of Uyghur labor law on imported toys
text:
Rep. Chris Smith (R-N.J.) and Adrian Zenz wrote in an April 29 opinion piece that popular Labubu dolls sold in the United States may contain cotton produced through forced labor in China’s Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region.
The issue highlights concerns about supply chains linked to alleged human rights abuses and the effectiveness of U.S. laws designed to prevent products made with forced labor from entering American markets.
Smith and Zenz said independent testing found that most Labubu dolls purchased in the U.S. contained cotton traced directly to Xinjiang farms, as reported by The New York Times following a tip received by Campaign for Uyghurs in 2025. They argued that under the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act, these products should have been stopped at the border. “Beijing’s repression of Uyghurs is now so deeply embedded in China’s economy that even trendy toys on American shelves are implicated,” they said.
Pop Mart, the company behind Labubu dolls, ended its partnership with Adidas after Adidas pledged not to use Xinjiang cotton due to forced labor concerns. Pop Mart defended its use of this cotton in Chinese court filings, saying Adidas had “baselessly smeared Xinjiang for violations of human rights” and “seriously hurt the feelings of the Chinese people.” The authors also cited research showing more than 90 percent of China’s cotton comes from Xinjiang, making it difficult to maintain clean supply chains within China.
A former Han Chinese police officer described supervising groups of Uyghurs forced to harvest cotton under security measures designed to prevent escape, with those refusing work sent to detention facilities until they complied. Research from the Victims of Communism Memorial Foundation identified up to 2.5 million people at risk of coerced work in what it called “the world’s largest system of state-imposed forced labor,” according to official sources cited by Smith and Zenz.
Smith has served as a member of Congress representing New Jersey’s 4th district since replacing Frank Thompson in 1981 according to official records . He was born in Rahway, New Jersey, is currently aged 70, lives in Manchester Township as reported by NJ.com , and graduated from The College of New Jersey with a Bachelor’s degree according to his alma mater .
In their article, Smith and Zenz urged Customs and Border Protection officials to stop imports tied to Pop Mart manufacturing hubs for further testing and called on authorities to add Pop Mart subsidiaries involved with forced labor-linked goods onto federal watch lists.

The issue highlights concerns about supply chains linked to alleged human rights abuses and the effectiveness of U.S. laws designed to prevent products made with forced labor from entering American markets.
